nodes.label: Failover Interception Model
nodes.rationale: On success the result is serialised to the store; on any exception the last stored result for the same arguments is returned so the caller sees stale-but-valid data instead of an error. If nothing is stored the exception is re-thrown (default) or null returned per exception policy.

nodes.label: Spring Proxy Requirement
nodes.rationale: Works with any Spring-container-managed AOP-proxied bean (Feign clients, @Service, @Component, @Repository, Spring Data repositories, @RestController) but the method must be invoked through the proxy, not via this.method() inside the same class. Plain Java objects are invisible to both the aspect and the scanner.

nodes.label: Optional Referential / ReferentialAware Model
nodes.rationale: No domain-model change is required; extending Referential or implementing ReferentialAware is optional and only adds upToDate, asOf and metadata so callers can distinguish live from stale data.

nodes.label: Store Choice in Production
nodes.rationale: Use JDBC in production: it persists across restarts, works across multiple instances, and is the only store supporting schema-level multi-tenancy. INMEMORY and CAFFEINE lose data on restart and belong in local development or tests.

nodes.label: Exception Policy (RETHROW / NEVER_THROW / custom)
nodes.rationale: RETHROW (default) re-throws the original exception on store miss; NEVER_THROW returns null or the RecoveredPayloadHandler result. All Throwables trigger recovery with no type filtering; narrowing that requires a custom FailoverExecution or the RESILIENCE type with a Resilience4j predicate.

nodes.label: MethodExceptionPolicy
nodes.rationale: Registered with failover.exception-policy: custom to wrap or translate the exception thrown on total failure, receiving a MethodExceptionContext carrying recoveredResult() and cause().

nodes.label: RecoveredPayloadHandler
nodes.rationale: Returns a default or sentinel value instead of null on store miss; can also be used to increment a recovery counter for monitoring.

nodes.label: Jackson Payload Serialisation
nodes.rationale: Payloads are JSON via Jackson with PAYLOAD_CLASS holding the FQCN for deserialisation, so domain types need a public no-arg constructor or @JsonCreator, readable fields, and no unresolvable type references. Renamed or removed fields break recovery of already-stored rows.

nodes.label: PayloadColumnResolver
nodes.rationale: For payloads exceeding VARCHAR(4000): either change the DDL to TEXT/CLOB or implement PayloadColumnResolver returning Types.CLOB from payloadType() and reading via getClob().

nodes.label: FAILOVER_STORE Table
nodes.rationale: Columns FAILOVER_NAME, FAILOVER_KEY, AS_OF, EXPIRE_ON, PAYLOAD, PAYLOAD_CLASS with primary key (FAILOVER_NAME, FAILOVER_KEY); the table name carries the failover.store.jdbc.table-prefix. The compound primary key is what makes concurrent multi-instance upserts safe.

nodes.label: Store Key Derivation
nodes.rationale: The default KeyGenerator joins all method arguments' toString() and MD5-hashes them into a fixed-length UUID-based key; the compound lookup is (name, key). Adding an argument silently changes the key so old entries stop matching — a custom KeyGenerator excluding it preserves backward compatibility. Different names never share entries regardless of argument overlap.

nodes.label: ExpiryCleanupScheduler
nodes.rationale: Runs on failover.scheduler.cleanup-cron (hourly by default) deleting rows where EXPIRE_ON < now, so the store does not grow without bound. Disable only when cleanup is managed externally, e.g. to batch deletes with a cursor and avoid lock contention.

nodes.label: Expired Entry Semantics
nodes.rationale: An expired entry is treated exactly like a missing one — it is never returned even if the row physically exists; the framework returns null or re-throws per the exception policy.

nodes.label: Async Store Write Trade-offs
nodes.rationale: Every success pays serialisation plus an insert/upsert; async offloads it so the caller is not blocked, and a store failure on the write path is logged without propagating. The costs: writes can be dropped when the test context shuts down first, and there is no exactly-once guarantee — concurrent writes for the same (name, key) race and the native upsert resolves last-write-wins with no distributed lock, which is acceptable for idempotent referential data.

nodes.label: TABLE_PREFIX vs SCHEMA Multi-tenancy
nodes.rationale: TABLE_PREFIX gives each tenant its own table via failover.store.multitenant.tenants. SCHEMA gives each tenant its own schema through a TenantStoreFactory bean and requires failover.store.async=false, because thread-local schema switching (e.g. SET search_path) is not carried by background async threads — otherwise connection leaks and wrong-schema errors appear.

nodes.label: DatabaseResolver and Silent Fallback
nodes.rationale: DefaultDatabaseResolver reads the product name from JDBC metadata; if metadata access is restricted or the name is unexpected, resolve() returns null, the merge query is disabled, and the store silently uses INSERT + UPDATE. A hardcoded DatabaseResolver bean forces the correct dialect.

nodes.label: PayloadSplitter Partial Recovery
nodes.rationale: Use it when a method returns a collection but entries should be stored per element, so if three of five items are stored those three are still returned with the upstream fully down. Each scatter slot dispatches on its own virtual thread, so thread-local security/tenant/trace context needs a ContextPropagator.

nodes.label: ObservablePublisher
nodes.rationale: Implemented to receive failover metrics and forward them to Micrometer, Prometheus, Datadog or another backend.

nodes.label: GraalVM Native Image Support
nodes.rationale: Not officially tested; Jackson serialisation and Spring AOP proxy generation are the concerns. Boot's native support handles AOP proxies but reflection-based domain deserialisation may need explicit Jackson type hints.

nodes.label: Recovery Troubleshooting Checklist
nodes.rationale: When recovery unexpectedly misses: key mismatch between store and recover arguments, expired EXPIRE_ON, wrong @Failover name, or an async write race. Enable DEBUG on com.societegenerale.failover to log the generated key on every store and recover call, and set failover.store.async=false in tests.

nodes.label: Duplicate Failover Name Startup Failure
nodes.rationale: Two annotations sharing a name would collide in the store and overwrite each other's entries on recovery, so startup fails with a duplicate-name error to prevent it.

nodes.label: Prefer a Real Store in Behaviour Tests
nodes.rationale: Mock the store only when testing an SPI implementation in isolation; for end-to-end failover behaviour use the real JDBC store on H2, because mocking skips serialisation, key derivation, expiry and enrichment — where most integration issues actually occur.
